title: Grand Palace & Temples Tour with Private Chauffeur
metaDescription: See the Grand Palace, Wat Pho and Wat Arun with a private chauffeur: early start, cool car between temples and no touts or taxi queues. Book on WhatsApp.
h1: The Grand Palace and Temple Circuit
bestTime: Depart 7:45 am, to be at the palace gates as they open
intro: Bangkok's three most celebrated sights, the Grand Palace, Wat Pho and Wat Arun, sit within a short distance of each other on either bank of the Chao Phraya. With a private chauffeur, you see all three in a single cool, unhurried morning.

sections.h2: Why go early, and why go by car
paragraphs: The Grand Palace opens at 8:30 am, and the first hour is by far the most pleasant. By late morning the tour coaches have arrived, the courtyards are full and the white marble radiates heat. Starting early means you enjoy the Emerald Buddha and the palace buildings in relative calm.

A chauffeur takes you to the visitor entrance on Na Phra Lan Road, then waits nearby. When you leave, the car is ready with cold water and air-conditioning. There is no bargaining with tuk-tuks, no searching for a taxi and no long walk around the palace walls in the midday sun.
It also keeps you clear of the well-known scam outside the gates, where friendly strangers claim the palace is closed and offer an alternative tour. With your own driver, you simply walk past.

sections.h2: Wat Pho and the Reclining Buddha
paragraphs: Just south of the palace, Wat Pho is home to the vast gilded Reclining Buddha, its feet inlaid with mother-of-pearl. The temple grounds are filled with chedis, statues and quiet courtyards, and Wat Pho is also regarded as the birthplace of traditional Thai massage, with a school still operating on site.
If you would like a massage, ask your chauffeur to allow extra time. It is a memorable way to rest your feet between temples.
Wat Pho is generally less crowded than the palace, and its shaded galleries of seated Buddhas make a peaceful contrast after the grandeur next door. Allow an hour to do it justice.

sections.h2: Across the river to Wat Arun
paragraphs: From Tha Tien pier beside Wat Pho, a short ferry crosses to Wat Arun, the Temple of Dawn, with its porcelain-studded spires. The crossing takes only a few minutes and is part of the experience.

While you cross by boat, your chauffeur drives round by bridge and meets you on the Thonburi side, so you do not need to return the way you came. Climb the lower terraces for views across the river towards the palace, then step straight into the car.

The Grand Palace has the strictest dress code in the country. Shoulders and knees must be covered, and sleeveless tops, shorts, short skirts, ripped jeans and tight or see-through clothing are not allowed. Comfortable shoes that slip off easily are ideal, as you will remove them in temple halls. A personal assistant can accompany you to handle tickets and queues, and families find the Alphard ideal for resting between stops.

title: Floating Markets Day Trip with Private Chauffeur
metaDescription: Private chauffeur to Damnoen Saduak floating market and Maeklong Railway Market: early start, flexible stops and a cool car between them. Book on WhatsApp.
h1: A Morning on the Floating Markets
bestTime: Depart 6:30 am, to reach the canals before the tour coaches
intro: West of Bangkok, the canals of Ratchaburi and Samut Songkhram still carry boats laden with fruit, noodles and flowers. With a private chauffeur, you arrive early, travel at your own pace and add the extraordinary Maeklong Railway Market to the same day.

paragraphs: Damnoen Saduak is the best known of Thailand's floating markets, about two hours from central Bangkok. It is undeniably popular with visitors, and by late morning the main canal is crowded with tour boats. Arrive early, though, and you will see vendors paddling boats piled with mangoes, coconuts and boat noodles in soft morning light.

Your chauffeur drops you at a reputable boat pier and waits while you explore by long-tail or paddle boat. Agree the boat price and duration before you board, and do not feel obliged to buy at every stop.
Most guests find an hour on the water is plenty, followed by a slow walk along the canal-side walkways to try fresh coconut ice cream or grilled snacks.

At Maeklong, a busy fresh market is set directly on the railway tracks. Several times a day, a train inches through, and vendors calmly fold back their awnings and pull their produce clear before setting everything back up moments later.
Train times can change, so we plan your morning around the current schedule. Your chauffeur will make sure you arrive in good time to find a safe spot to watch, then collect you nearby afterwards.

Between trains, Maeklong is a working market where local families shop for fish, vegetables and curry pastes. It is a fascinating glimpse of everyday life, and a contrast to the more tourist-oriented canals of Damnoen Saduak.

sections.h2: Why a private car makes sense
paragraphs: Group tours follow fixed schedules and often include long shopping stops. A private chauffeur lets you decide how long to stay at each market, when to have lunch and when to return. You can visit a traditional coconut-sugar workshop, stop at a roadside fruit stall or skip anything that does not appeal.
Bangkok's outbound traffic can be heavy, so an early start matters. The return journey is relaxed, and you can rest in the car on the way back to your hotel.

Comfort counts on a day like this. Your chauffeur keeps the car cool, carries cold water and towels, and will stop whenever you need a break. Children can nap on the way home, and the generous luggage space holds any fruit, crafts or souvenirs you collect along the way.

On Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays, Amphawa Floating Market adds a more local, Thai-style experience in the afternoon and evening. A personal assistant can translate and help you buy, and the Alphard's space is ideal for families with children.

title: ICONSIAM & Riverside Evening with Private Chauffeur
metaDescription: An evening at ICONSIAM, Lhong 1919 and Asiatique with a private chauffeur: sunset by the river, dinner and an easy ride home. Book on WhatsApp today.
h1: ICONSIAM and the River at Dusk
bestTime: Pick-up 4 pm, to catch golden hour on the river
intro: As the sun drops, the Chao Phraya glows and the riverbanks come alive. This evening combines heritage, shopping and the city's most impressive riverfront mall, with your chauffeur waiting at every stop.

sections.h2: Begin in the old trading houses
paragraphs: Lhong 1919, on the Thonburi bank, is a restored Chinese trading house built around a courtyard, with a shrine to the sea goddess Mazu, murals and small shops. It is calm in the late afternoon and a lovely introduction to the river's history.
Your chauffeur drops you at the entrance and repositions to ICONSIAM, a short drive away, so the next stop is effortless.

Across the river, the old Customs House and Charoen Krung's galleries recall the era when this stretch was Bangkok's gateway to the world. The view from Lhong 1919's riverside deck takes in both banks, a fitting start to an evening that crosses between them.

ICONSIAM is one of Asia's most ambitious shopping centres. Its ground floor houses SookSiam, an indoor floating-market concept showcasing food and crafts from Thailand's regions, while the upper levels hold international luxury houses, Thai designers and restaurants with river views.

Outside, the riverside park is the place to watch the sunset over the water. On many evenings the mall stages a multimedia fountain show along the river; times vary, so we will check the schedule for your visit.
ICONSIAM's driveways get very busy in the evening. Your chauffeur will agree a pick-up point with you, so you can leave when you choose without joining the queues.

The Gold Line, a short automated monorail, links ICONSIAM to the BTS, but at the end of an evening with shopping bags in hand most guests are glad of a car waiting at the door rather than a crowded platform.

For dinner, you could stay at ICONSIAM, cross to one of the grand hotels along Charoen Krung or board a dinner cruise. Our personal assistant service can help request reservations and cruise bookings, subject to availability.
If you take a cruise, your chauffeur will meet you at the pier where it returns, so there is no need to find transport late in the evening.
Prefer something quieter? A hotel terrace on the Thonburi bank offers views straight across to the illuminated skyline, and your chauffeur can take you there directly from ICONSIAM.

End the evening at Asiatique The Riverfront, a night market in restored warehouses with a large Ferris wheel. It is lively until late, and when you are ready to leave, your car is waiting at the entrance. A five-hour booking covers most of this evening, and extra hours can be added if you choose to linger.

title: Chatuchak Weekend Market with Private Chauffeur
metaDescription: Shop Chatuchak Weekend Market with a private chauffeur: early start, bag drops at the car, Or Tor Kor breakfast and a cool ride home. Book on WhatsApp.
bestTime: Saturday or Sunday, arrive by 9:30 am, before the heat
intro: Chatuchak is one of the world's largest weekend markets, a maze of thousands of stalls selling everything from vintage clothing and ceramics to plants and street food. A private chauffeur turns it from an endurance test into a pleasure.

sections.h2: Start with breakfast at Or Tor Kor
paragraphs: Across the road from Chatuchak, Or Tor Kor is one of Bangkok's finest fresh markets, known for immaculate displays of tropical fruit, curries, sweets and prepared dishes. It is a perfect place for breakfast and a gentle introduction to Thai flavours.
Your chauffeur drops you at the entrance and then moves to the agreed meeting point at Chatuchak, so you can stroll over when you are ready.

Or Tor Kor opens early every day, so you avoid the weekend rush at Chatuchak's own food stalls. It is also an excellent place to buy premium mangoes, durian and Thai sweets to take back to your hotel, which your chauffeur can keep cool in the car.

Chatuchak is divided into numbered sections, each loosely themed: clothing, homeware, ceramics, art, antiques, pets and plants. The central clock tower is the best landmark, and a market map helps you plan your route.

The lanes are narrow and busy, and the heat builds quickly under the metal roofs. The market typically opens around 9 am, and the first hours are the most comfortable. By early afternoon the crowds are at their peak.
Many guests enjoy taking a personal assistant along, who can help with translation, bargaining and carrying, and who knows which sections suit your interests.

Prices are generally fixed for small items, but polite bargaining is acceptable for larger purchases. A smile and a reasonable offer go a long way, and many sellers will happily package fragile goods for travel.

The biggest benefit of a private chauffeur at Chatuchak is simple: you do not have to carry everything. Message your chauffeur, meet at an agreed gate and hand over your purchases. Then continue shopping with free hands.
Larger items, such as ceramics, artwork or furniture, can be stored safely in the car. The Alphard's generous luggage space is ideal for a serious shopping trip.

Some larger stalls can arrange international shipping for bulky items such as furniture. If you plan to ship home, a personal assistant can help you compare options and handle the paperwork, while your chauffeur takes care of the smaller pieces.

A five-hour chauffeur comfortably covers Or Tor Kor and a long morning at Chatuchak. If you want to continue to lunch elsewhere or visit other parts of the city, a ten-hour booking gives you more freedom. Shoppers with high-value purchases may prefer a discreet bodyguard alongside them.

title: Bangkok Rooftop Bars Night with Private Chauffeur
metaDescription: Bangkok's best rooftop bars with a private chauffeur: Mahanakhon SkyWalk, Vertigo, Sky Bar and Octave, car waiting between each. Book on WhatsApp now.
bestTime: Pick-up 5:30 pm, to be high above the city at sunset
intro: Few cities do rooftops like Bangkok. This evening takes you from a glass-floored observation deck at sunset to some of the city's most celebrated sky-high bars, with a chauffeur gliding you between them.

paragraphs: Begin at King Power Mahanakhon, whose pixelated tower rises above Sathorn and Silom. The SkyWalk observation deck, among the highest in Bangkok, includes a glass floor for the brave and an open-air rooftop bar to watch the sun set.
Your chauffeur drops you at the entrance and waits nearby, ready to move on as the city lights up below.

Tickets for the SkyWalk are bought at the tower, and the queue is usually shortest in the late afternoon. Aim to be at the top about half an hour before sunset, so you can see the city in daylight, at golden hour and then lit up after dark.

Vertigo, on the rooftop of Banyan Tree Bangkok, is one of the city's best-known open-air restaurants, with uninterrupted views in every direction. The adjoining Moon Bar is ideal for a drink if you would prefer a lighter evening. Reservations are recommended, and our personal assistant service can help request a table, subject to availability.
Weather matters on any rooftop. In heavy rain, open-air venues may close or move service indoors. Your chauffeur follows conditions and can adjust the plan, suggesting covered alternatives if needed.
The dry, cooler months from November to February are the most reliable for rooftop evenings, but even in the rainy season, showers often pass quickly and leave clear, fresh skies behind them.

Sky Bar at lebua at State Tower is perhaps Bangkok's most famous rooftop, its golden dome and curving bar overlooking the river. It is busy, glamorous and has a strict dress code: smart casual, with no shorts, sleeveless shirts for men or open sandals.
Later, cross to Sukhumvit for Octave at the Bangkok Marriott Hotel Sukhumvit, whose multi-level terraces offer sweeping views across the eastern city. It is relaxed and stays open late.
If you are still hungry afterwards, Thonglor is only a few minutes away, with late-night noodle shops and izakayas. Your chauffeur knows where to find them and will wait outside while you eat.

sections.h2: Why a chauffeur makes the night
paragraphs: Rooftop bars are spread across Sathorn, Silom and Sukhumvit, and the traffic between them can be slow. With a chauffeur, there is no waiting for taxis in your best clothes, and you are never left on a busy street late at night. A five-hour booking covers this evening comfortably; add hours if you want to linger. High-profile guests can add a discreet bodyguard for the evening.

h1: An Evening of Bangkok Fine Dining
bestTime: Pick-up 6:30 pm, after the worst of the evening rush
intro: Bangkok has become one of Asia's great dining capitals, with chefs reinterpreting Thai cooking alongside world-class European tables. This evening pairs an aperitif, a tasting menu and a nightcap, with a chauffeur taking care of every journey in between.

paragraphs: Start at the Bamboo Bar at the Mandarin Oriental, a riverside institution with live jazz, or at a hotel bar of your choice. It is the perfect place to settle into the evening while the city's traffic eases.
Your chauffeur drops you at the hotel entrance and waits nearby. When it is time for dinner, the car is ready, so you never arrive flustered or late for a table that may have taken weeks to secure.

If you are staying on the Sukhumvit side, a hotel bar closer to your restaurant works just as well. Tell us where you are dining and we will suggest an aperitif stop that keeps the evening's driving short.

Bangkok's Michelin Guide includes a remarkable range of restaurants. Some reinterpret regional Thai cooking, such as Sorn, with its focus on Southern Thai cuisine, or Nusara, facing Wat Pho in the Old Town. Others are progressive, such as Gaggan Anand, or rooted in European traditions, such as Le Normandie at the Mandarin Oriental or Côte at Capella Bangkok. Potong, in a restored Chinatown shophouse, blends Thai and Chinese influences.

Many of these restaurants are booked well in advance. Our personal assistant service can help request reservations, note dietary requirements and coordinate timings, though availability is always at each restaurant's discretion.

Tasting menus can last three hours or more, and the best dining rooms are spread across the city, from the riverside to Sukhumvit and the Old Town. That is exactly why a chauffeur is so useful on a night like this.

After dinner, continue to one of the city's acclaimed cocktail bars. BKK Social Club at the Four Seasons Hotel Bangkok at Chao Phraya River is elegant and polished, while the small bars around Soi Nana in Chinatown offer a more intimate atmosphere.
Your chauffeur will take you there and then home, so you can enjoy the wine pairing without a second thought about how you will get back.

Most fine-dining restaurants ask for smart casual dress. Men may prefer closed shoes and long trousers, and some venues discourage shorts and sandals. Arrive on time, as tasting menus are often served to a schedule.

Choose a five-hour booking for a single restaurant and nightcap, or add hours if you plan to linger. For a celebration, the Rowen Vellfire Z or Porsche Cayenne S makes a memorable arrival, and a discreet bodyguard can accompany high-profile guests.

h1: A Night at the Muay Thai
bestTime: Pick-up 5:30 pm, for dinner before the first bout
intro: Muay Thai is Thailand's national sport, and nothing compares to watching it live in one of Bangkok's historic stadiums. With a private chauffeur, you enjoy the ritual, the music and the noise, then step straight into a waiting car.

paragraphs: Rajadamnern Stadium, on Ratchadamnoen Nok Avenue near the Old Town, is one of the oldest and most storied Muay Thai venues in the country, dating back to the 1940s. Its circular arena is intimate and atmospheric.

Lumpinee Boxing Stadium, the other great name, moved in 2014 from its original site near Lumphini Park to a modern arena on Ram Intra Road in the north of the city. It is a longer drive from central hotels, which makes a chauffeur especially useful.
Both stadiums hold regular fight nights, though schedules vary through the week and over the year. We will check the current fight card and suggest the best evening for your visit.

Some evenings feature televised promotions with modern staging and lighting, while others feel more traditional. Both are exciting; tell us whether you would prefer spectacle or atmosphere, and we will point you to the right night.

Each fight begins with the wai kru ram muay, a ritual dance in which fighters honour their teachers, accompanied by traditional music of oboe, drums and cymbals. The music continues through each round, rising in tempo as the action intensifies.

A typical card includes several bouts, building towards a main event. Ringside seats bring you close to the action, while the upper tiers are where you will find the loudest, most passionate local fans.

Bouts are usually five rounds, though some promotions use shorter formats. Between rounds, watch the corners: trainers work quickly with water, ice and advice, and the crowd's reactions tell you who is winning long before the judges' decision is announced.

Before the fights at Rajadamnern, a short drive takes you to Thip Samai on Maha Chai Road, one of Bangkok's best-known pad Thai restaurants. The queue moves quickly, and the setting is wonderfully local.
We can help arrange ringside tickets where available, and a personal assistant can accompany you to explain the rules and the ritual. Tickets are also sold at the stadiums.
If you are heading to Lumpinee instead, your chauffeur can suggest a dinner stop closer to Ram Intra, so the evening flows without a long detour across the city.

When the final bout ends, crowds spill out onto the street and taxis disappear. Your chauffeur meets you at an agreed point and takes you straight back to your hotel. A five-hour booking covers dinner and a full card.
Guests who prefer extra reassurance in crowded venues can add a discreet bodyguard, and the Alphard's space suits groups of friends who want to travel together.

title: Bangkok Golf Day with Private Chauffeur
metaDescription: A Bangkok golf day with a private chauffeur: early pick-up, room for clubs, transfers to top courses near the city and a relaxed return. Book on WhatsApp.
h1: A Bangkok Golf Day, Done Properly
kicker: Bangkok Experience · Courses Around the Capital
bestTime: Depart 5:30 am, to tee off before the midday heat
intro: Some of Asia's finest golf courses lie within easy reach of Bangkok. With a private chauffeur, you leave before dawn, arrive relaxed and return without worrying about traffic, clubs or a post-round drink.

paragraphs: Popular courses include Thai Country Club, east of the city off the Bang Na–Trat road and long regarded as one of the country's most polished clubs; Alpine Golf Club, north of Bangkok in Pathum Thani; and Nikanti Golf Club, west of the city in Nakhon Pathom, known for its inclusive day format and distinctive layout.

Each lies roughly an hour or so from central Bangkok, depending on traffic and the time of day. Your chauffeur plans the fastest route via the expressway network and gets you there with time for breakfast and the range.
We can help arrange tee times subject to each club's availability and policies. Some clubs have visitor restrictions or require booking through members or partners, so it is worth planning ahead.

Thailand's heat builds steadily from late morning, and the best conditions are in the first few hours after sunrise. An early tee time means you play in cooler air and finish before the afternoon storms that often arrive in the rainy season.
Leaving Bangkok early also avoids the morning rush. Your chauffeur collects you at 5:30 am, with coffee on request, and you can rest in the car on the way.
In the cooler months from November to February, mornings can be genuinely pleasant, and a later tee time is possible. During the hot season from March to May, an early start makes a real difference.

Caddies are standard at Thai golf courses and are usually required. They know every green and are an important part of the experience; tipping your caddie is customary. Most clubs ask for collared shirts and tailored shorts or trousers, with no denim.
Your chauffeur waits at the clubhouse throughout your round, so your clubs, bags and change of clothes are always safe.

Many clubs offer excellent clubhouse facilities, from locker rooms and spas to restaurants serving Thai and international dishes. There is no rush to leave; your chauffeur will be ready whenever you are.

For one or two golfers, the Toyota Camry carries two golf bags comfortably. For a four-ball, an Alphard or Vellfire offers space for players and clubs, or we can arrange two vehicles. After the round, enjoy lunch and a drink at the clubhouse before a relaxed drive back to Bangkok.
A ten-hour booking covers the full day, including travel. A personal assistant can coordinate tee times and arrangements for groups.

Help arranging tee times at popular courses
Space for clubs and bags in every vehicle
Chauffeur waits at the clubhouse all day
Relaxed return after lunch and drinks

Caddies are usually compulsory; tipping is customary.

title: Ayutthaya Day Trip with Private Chauffeur
metaDescription: An Ayutthaya day trip with a private chauffeur: Bang Pa-In palace, temple ruins, river prawn lunch and a cool car between every site. Book on WhatsApp.
kicker: Bangkok Day Trip · Ayutthaya Historical Park
bestTime: Depart 7:30 am, before the heat and tour buses
intro: For more than four centuries, Ayutthaya was the capital of the Siamese kingdom and one of the great cities of Asia. Its temple ruins, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site, lie about an hour and a half north of Bangkok.

paragraphs: Begin at the Bang Pa-In Royal Palace, on the way to Ayutthaya. This elegant complex of European, Chinese and Thai-style buildings sits around ornamental lakes and gardens, and is a beautiful place to stroll in the morning.
Bang Pa-In has a strict dress code: shoulders and knees must be covered, and visitors in shorts or sleeveless tops may be refused entry or asked to rent appropriate clothing.

The palace grounds are best enjoyed slowly. Look out for the Chinese-style Wehart Chamrun hall, the elegant pavilion in the middle of the lake and the observatory tower, which offers views across the gardens.

sections.h2: The temples of the island city
paragraphs: Ayutthaya's historic centre sits on an island ringed by rivers. At Wat Mahathat, you will find the famous Buddha head entwined in the roots of a fig tree, one of Thailand's most photographed sights. Please keep your head lower than the Buddha's when taking photos.
Nearby, Wat Phra Si Sanphet's three great chedis once stood within the royal palace grounds, and the neighbouring Wihan Phra Mongkhon Bophit houses one of Thailand's largest bronze Buddha images.

The temples are spread out, unshaded and hot by late morning. Your chauffeur drives you between them and waits at each entrance with cold water and air-conditioning, so you see far more without exhausting yourself.

Ayutthaya was sacked in 1767, and the ruins you see today bear the scars of that destruction: headless Buddha images, toppled chedis and weathered brick. It is a moving place, and many visitors find it the most memorable part of their time in Thailand.
Ayutthaya is famous for grilled giant river prawns, served at riverside restaurants around the island. It is a memorable lunch and a chance to rest before the afternoon.
Afterwards, visit Wat Chaiwatthanaram, a majestic Khmer-style temple on the west bank of the Chao Phraya, especially atmospheric in the softer afternoon light.

If time allows, Wat Yai Chai Mongkhon, with its tall chedi and rows of saffron-draped Buddha images, and the reclining Buddha at Wat Lokayasutharam are both worthwhile additions. Your chauffeur can fit them in on the way back to the main road.
Group tours follow fixed timetables and often spend long periods at shopping stops. With a private chauffeur, you choose how long to stay at each temple, add or skip sites and set your own pace.

A ten-hour booking covers the full day, including travel. A personal assistant can act as guide and translator, explaining the history, and families appreciate the space of an Alphard after long walks in the heat.

Buddha head in the tree at Wat Mahathat
Wat Phra Si Sanphet's three great chedis

tips: Cover shoulders and knees, especially for Bang Pa-In Palace.
Keep your head lower than the Buddha head at Wat Mahathat for photos.
Bring a hat, sunscreen and comfortable shoes; the ruins are unshaded.

faqs.q: How far is Ayutthaya from Bangkok?
faqs.a: About 80 kilometres, or roughly an hour and a half by car, depending on traffic.

faqs.q: What should I wear?
faqs.a: Cover your shoulders and knees. Bang Pa-In Palace enforces a strict dress code.

faqs.q: Are entrance fees included?
faqs.a: Entrance fees are paid at each site. A personal assistant can help with tickets.

faqs.q: Can we return by boat?
faqs.a: River cruises between Ayutthaya and Bangkok exist; we can help you explore the options, with your chauffeur meeting you at the end.

title: Luxury Shopping Day in Bangkok with Private Chauffeur
metaDescription: A Bangkok luxury shopping day with a private chauffeur: Central Embassy, Gaysorn, Siam Paragon and EmQuartier, purchases secure in the car. Book now.
h1: A Day of Bangkok Luxury Shopping
bestTime: Start 10 am, as the boutiques open
intro: Bangkok is one of Asia's great shopping cities, with flagship boutiques, Thai designers and department stores within a few kilometres of each other. A private chauffeur makes it a day of pleasure rather than a test of stamina.

paragraphs: Start at Central Embassy, home to many of the world's leading fashion houses and the Park Hyatt above. Then continue to Gaysorn Village, connected by skywalk, which mixes international labels with Thai designers and elegant cafés.
Your chauffeur waits nearby, stores your purchases securely and meets you at whichever entrance you choose. When your hands are full, you simply message and the car is waiting.
Central Chidlom, a short drive along Ploenchit Road, is a classic Thai department store with an excellent food hall and beauty floor, if you have a list of gifts to buy.

For lunch, the Erawan Tea Room at the Grand Hyatt Erawan offers a calm setting overlooking the Ratchaprasong intersection. Then a short drive takes you to Siam Paragon, one of Bangkok's best-known malls, with luxury maisons, watch and jewellery boutiques and an excellent gourmet market.
If you prefer, ICONSIAM on the river offers another luxury destination, and your chauffeur can adapt the route at any time.

Siam Paragon's watch and jewellery floors are popular with collectors, and Thai jewellery and silk make thoughtful gifts. Take your time; with a chauffeur, there is no reason to rush, and you can break for coffee or a spa treatment whenever you like.

In the afternoon, continue to EmQuartier and Emporium in Phrom Phong, where international brands sit alongside Thai labels and lifestyle stores. It is a good place to finish with a coffee or an early dinner.
By the end of the day, you may have many bags. Your chauffeur keeps them secure and organised, and the Alphard's luggage space means nothing is crowded or creased.
If you would rather not carry everything home, many stores can arrange delivery to your hotel. A personal assistant can coordinate deliveries and check that each item arrives safely before you leave.

For high-value purchases, you may prefer a discreet bodyguard to accompany you on foot, while your chauffeur stays with the car. A personal assistant can help with sizing, translation, delivery arrangements and VAT refund paperwork.

Visitors can usually claim back VAT on eligible purchases at participating stores. Ask for the refund form and present your passport when you pay, then follow the airport procedure before departure. Minimum spend thresholds apply.
A ten-hour booking covers a full day of shopping and dinner, with extra hours available if needed.
